key_insight: Double-pulse resistance spot welding improves nugget stability and mechanical performance by separating heating into a preheat, cooling interval, and main pulse.
engineering_relevance: The process is highly relevant for lightweight automotive and structural joints because it reduces expulsion, narrows the heat-affected zone, and performs better on AHSS, stainless steels, and dissimilar metals.
method: Apply a low-current preheating pulse to initiate controlled heating.
Insert an inter-pulse cooling phase to stabilize temperature rise.
Use a higher main pulse to complete nugget formation with improved consistency.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes reported comparisons showing DP-RSW generally yields better temperature control, more consistent nuggets, higher tensile shear strength/failure energy, and reduced expulsion versus single-pulse welding.
watch_item: Benefits depend on careful pulse timing and current control; poorly tuned schedules may still cause uneven heating or incomplete nugget formation.
paper_title: A comprehensive review of Double-Pulse resistance spot welding for enhanced weld quality and mechanical performance
